kicker: Metals · producers' EBITDA margins, Q2 FY27
title: Metal margins rose, except where ore had to be bought
title_em: except where ore had to be bought
dek: Five of eight listed metal producers widened Q2 FY27 EBITDA margins and two held within half a point. Godawari Power fell 7.9 points to 12.0% after a stalled captive mine forced it to buy iron ore at ₹3,300–3,500/t.

chart.title: EBITDA margin, Q2 FY26 → Q2 FY27
chart.sub: consolidated filed results · label shows Q2 FY27 margin

stats.label: Godawari Power's margin
stats.note: 12.0% from 19.9%; it cut FY27 mining guidance to 2.5 Mt from 3.4 Mt.

stats.label: SAIL's imported coking coal
stats.note: Up about ₹1,700/t on Q1; October steel realisation ran ~₹4,000/t above the Q2 average.

stats.label: Hindustan Copper's margin
stats.note: 59.8% from 39.3% as revenue rose 64%, the largest gain in the group.

read: Owning the ore was the margin edge in Q2; with coal costs still climbing, H2 margins depend on whether higher metal prices hold.
sources: Vantage analysis of Q2 FY27 results filed on BSE and Q2 FY27 earnings calls; Vantage sector intel, 21 Nov 2026
notes: EBITDA margin is operating EBITDA over revenue from operations in filed consolidated Q2 FY27 and Q2 FY26 results, as computed by Vantage; company-reported figures can differ (Hindalco reports business EBITDA of ₹13,869 cr; Lloyds reports a 37.2% standalone margin). Tata Steel's consolidated figure includes its European operations. Godawari's iron ore purchase price, mining guidance cut and the dumping-space constraint, SAIL's coking coal cost and October realisation, and Hindalco's roughly 5% quarter-on-quarter rise in aluminium cost on coal come from their Q2 FY27 calls. Hindustan Copper's call was not on the desk, so its margin gain is shown without a stated cause. Vedanta is left out because its demerger makes the year-ago comparison not like-for-like; JSW Steel and Jindal Steel results were not on the desk.
